stage3.sig: WEB to DB direct - microsegmentation bypass

summary.thesis_claim: Proposed agent escalates with kill-chain context (higher confidence, correlation markers present); SOAR correctly mitigates on SID match but cannot escalate, correlate across stages, or distinguish cold vs. sequence.

reasoning: SID 9000001 triggered on TCP SYN from WEB zone (10.1.100.10) to DB-OLTP zone (10.1.200.10) on PostgreSQL port 5432 - this is a hard microsegmentation violation per the policy matrix (WEB → DB-OLTP = DENY).

The flow violates the established application architecture: legitimate path is WEB → APP-GW (10.3.100.10:8080) → APP-CORE → DB-OLTP. Direct WEB→DB bypasses security controls and represents a crown-jewel exposure risk.
No baseline match exists for this flow - it is NOT in known production traffic patterns. The only legitimate WEB outbound is web-to-appgw-proxy (critical), which this targeted block preserves.

Source host (web-01) has a concerning history: 10 alerts in 30 days, trust score 0.36, with 4 prior SID 9000001 violations all enforced with DROP. Past decisions show 8/9 enforced, indicating a recurring threat pattern.
Multi-alert correlation shows kill-chain progression: recent SID sequence includes 9000001, 9000901, 9000905, 9000002 - suggesting a multi-stage attack campaign rather than isolated misconfiguration.

Threat pattern 'cross_zone_violation_web_to_db' matches with confidence anchor 0.95, MITRE TA0008/T1021. Severity scoring: cross_zone_policy_violation (+4) + dst_port_in_critical_db_set (+1) + corroborated_by_past_incidents (+1) = 6 points → P1.

Targeted block (src+dst+port) chosen over full-source block to preserve critical web-to-appgw-proxy flow while stopping the violation. Blast radius assessment confirms this is the minimal effective action.

Confidence 0.95 calibrated: unambiguous policy violation + zero FP scenarios in baseline + historical enforcement consistency + MITRE technique match. No hard overrides apply (src not in MGT, dst not in NEVER_BLOCK).

hypotheses.name: Lateral movement bypass
hypotheses.description: Lateral movement bypass (probability=0.95) — WEB host attempting direct DB access, bypassing the full application chain. Evidence: SID 9000001 trigger, policy matrix DENY, no baseline match, past enforcement pattern (4/4 enforced), multi-SID kill-chain signal. Counter: None significant - this is a hard microsegmentation violation with zero legitimate runtime use case.

hypotheses.name: Misconfigured monitoring tool
hypotheses.description: Misconfigured monitoring tool (probability=0.03) — A monitoring or health-check tool misconfigured to connect directly from WEB to DB. Evidence: None - no legitimate baseline exists for this path. Counter: Would have been documented in change management; trust score 0.36 suggests recurring violations; runtime reputation clean but past decisions show 8/9 enforced.

hypotheses.name: Pre-announced DB migration
hypotheses.description: Pre-announced DB migration (probability=0.02) — Emergency schema migration run from WEB host. Evidence: None - no change window documented. Counter: Should originate from MGT zone per policy; would be pre-communicated; FP scenarios explicitly listed as 'extremely rare' in threat playbook.
